title: Relative degreewise pseudo-coherence detected by affine derived sections
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], and fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, $R\Gamma(U,E|_U)\in D(A)$ denotes module-valued derived sections: derived direct image along the ringed-space map $(U,\mathcal O_U)\to(\{*\},A)$ given by global sections [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. On quasi-coherent complexes it is the quasi-inverse in [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. The following are equivalent: (1) $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]; (2) there are affine open covers $S=\bigcup_i V_i$ and $f^{-1}(V_i)=\bigcup_j U_{ij}$ such that $R\Gamma(U_{ij},E|_{U_{ij}})$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_S)$ [def-sfb-ring-relative-m-pseudocoherent]; (3) for every affine open pair $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, $R\Gamma(U,E|_U)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_S)$ [def-sfb-ring-relative-m-pseudocoherent]. The algebra structure is always the one induced by $f$. Covers and polynomial presentations may depend on $m$; no Noetherian or global boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix an affine pair $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $A$ is a finite type $R$-algebra. Choosing finitely many generators gives a surjection $\alpha:P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$. The affine description of relative affine space [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] and the quotient-ring characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] identify this with a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow T=\mathbf A^n_V=\operatorname{Spec}P$. Conversely any such immersion gives such a surjection. Keep the algebra actions induced by these maps throughout.

source.place: Tag 09VF proof, choosing an affine pair and polynomial embedding

proof.text: Put $M=R\Gamma(U,E|_U)\in D(A)$. By [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], choose a representative module complex $M^\bullet$ so that its termwise associated sheaf complex $F^\bullet=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ represents $E|_U$. Every term of $F^\bullet$ is quasi-coherent. Choose a K-injective resolution $s:F^\bullet\to J^\bullet$; by [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], $Ri_*(E|_U)$ is represented by $i_*J^\bullet$. The morphism $i$ is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion], so [lem-pc-affine-pushforward-resolution-quasi-iso] makes $i_*s$ a quasi-isomorphism, with no boundedness requirement. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec] gives a natural module-sheaf isomorphism $i_*\widetilde{M^q}\cong\widetilde{\operatorname{Res}_\alpha M^q}$ for every term; naturality makes these commute with all differentials. Thus, in $D(\mathcal O_T)$, we obtain $$Ri_*(E|_U)\cong\widetilde{\operatorname{Res}_\alpha M}.$$ This is an isomorphism of structure-module derived objects, with the $P$-action through $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 09VF proof, identification of the closed pushforward with the associated scalar-restricted module complex

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-m-pseudocoherent-criterion] over $P$ to the isomorphism in step 2. It says that $Ri_*(E|_U)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent exactly when $\operatorname{Res}_\alpha M$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $P$. Isomorphisms preserve the approximation condition: compose the approximating morphism with the isomorphism; the induced cohomology isomorphisms and surjectivity are unchanged. Taking the existential quantifier over $n$ and $\alpha$ therefore identifies existence of a good polynomial embedding for $(U,V,E|_U)$ with relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of $M$ over $R$, by [def-sfb-ring-relative-m-pseudocoherent]. This uses the same polynomial presentation on the two sides, so no change-of-presentation theorem is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 09VF proof, final comparison using Tag 08E7 and the algebraic definition

proof.text: Apply step 3 on each pair in a chosen affine covering. The existential covering-and-embedding condition defining (1) in [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] becomes exactly (2), proving (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2). If (1) holds, [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-all-affine-charts] says that for every affine pair and every polynomial closed embedding its pushforward is $m$-pseudo-coherent, and also supplies an embedding for each pair. Step 3 then gives the module condition for every pair, namely (3). Finally (3) implies (2) by choosing an affine cover of $S$ and affine covers of its inverse images in $X$. These exist by the affine-open basis property [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. All choices are made for the fixed integer $m$; no uniform cover as $m$ varies and no global cohomological bound is used.

source.place: Tag 09VF proof, formal assembly using Tag 09UJ
